findings.reason: the section needs either those production paths granted or the two ids pre-declared as blocked-branch candidates, otherwise the node burns its gate and lands seven of nine while reporting a scope defect.
findings.text:
the write paths grant only the nine test files plus `reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py` and `reckon/crew/station_store.py`, but two of the nine ids fail in production code those paths exclude: `tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py::test_every_crew_verb_help_names_its_state_or_condition` fails because the new `retention-sweep` verb (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1558`) has no entry in `STATE_PHRASES`, and the test asserts the phrase appears in the command's own first help line, so the row cannot be added without editing that verb's docstring; and `tests/test_crew_path_prints_the_resolved_home.py::test_a_selector_a_kind_does_not_take_is_refused` fails because `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:410-425` lets `--kind live --project

--run ` through and exits 0 (verify.log:513-527), where the test's whole property is that a selector the kind does not take is refused. A node on this section can only re-freeze those two tests into asserting the defect (deleting the invariant) or block the ids, so the Done-when is unreachable inside the granted scope

findings.reason: naming the control for that id (delete the module, or disable the allowlist entry, and show the id fails) removes an ambiguity that otherwise invites a nominal control.
findings.text: the negative control is "mutate the production code the test pins … restoring the old expectation is not a control", but for `test_every_module_is_reached` the repair itself is an `ALLOWLIST` row (the section's own added sentence) and the only falsification the node can perform in scope is removing that row or deleting the module, neither of which is the production mutation the sentence describes, so this id's control is left ambiguous

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `c8a082c99`, `684c1caa6` and `73decd0f4` all resolve and `73decd0f4` is the commit that first put the `plan-review-of-` literal in `reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py`; the cited module facts hold at HEAD (`reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py:147` holds the single constant, `reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py:14` spells it again, `reckon/crew/station_store.py:200` calls `date.fromisoformat`), and both owner-plan slugs resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the nine-id negative control is per-id and forbids "restoring the old expectation", but for the one id repaired by an ALLOWLIST row (`tests/test_every_module_is_reached.py::test_every_module_is_reached`) no in-scope production mutation is named, and the only obvious mutation is the row itself, which is a test change.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — `~/.cache/reckon-suite-census/c8a082c99e3023b61c438143e898bd0039315149-rerun/rerun.log` and `~/.cache/reckon-suite-census/verify-684c1caa61836074490c2589abacf828be76a00a/verify.log` both exist and are durable; the section routes its own gate logs under the run directory and its arms through `git archive` on node-local disk.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section asks for one constant in `reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py` and names no plan label, stage name or ticket id as a symbol; `reckon._timestamps.parse_utc` is named as the mechanism, not a fix recipe.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the Deliverable's two exits (re-freeze the test, or block the id as unintended) do not produce the Done-when (all nine ids green) for the ids whose failure is a production defect outside the section's write paths; two ids are confirmed production-side in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, which the write paths do not grant.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §51 is one cause group ("a one-owner invariant acquiring a second spelling or an unreached module") like §41's fourteen ids and §46's twelve; each id carries its own commit read and block rule, and the section closes on one measure (the listed ids green, with blocked ids named).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §51 declares no cross-section dependency because none is needed (its test files are already green elsewhere in the plan, §40 is `done`, and the sections it could collide with edit different files); the two plans it names as owners both exist and both carry later `implementable` sections that consume the modules (`a-coordinator-sees-the-board` §5 at docs/plans/a-coordinator-sees-the-board.html:149, `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once` §6–§7 at docs/plans/the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once.html:172).
